clue.text: Money is lost by this sweep

parts.note: bread is slang for money

indicators.note: the word is goes missing from the word this, leaving two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gambler laments that a wide swing of fortune has cost him money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as money being lost on a bet; in fact 'is lost by this' strips IS from the word THIS, a neat piece of in-clue deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is an extent or range, the same as the width or scope of something.

clue.text: Sounds made by, say, grandfather's cane, heading for the back

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for a cane moves to the end, as a head going to the back

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

explanation.surface: An old man's walking cane makes tapping noises as he heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandfather means a grandfather clock, whose sounds are its regular beats; 'heading for the back' moves the S of STICK to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's mechanism makes regular clicking beats, the tick-tock of a longcase timepiece.

clue.text: Ferret's gone across singular sleeping place

indicators.note: the word for ferret spans the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: to ferret about is to root about, searching
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A pet ferret has wandered over to find a single place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle for the night is their place of rest.

clue.text: To stand side by side's a mere sham, first son being cross

indicators.note: the first S (son) in the phrase is swapped for X, the cross shape

parts.note: just a pose is a phrase for a mere sham or affectation

explanation.surface: Someone complains that standing together for show is fake, and an elder boy is angry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: JUST A POSE has its first S replaced by X, the cross: 'cross' is a noun here, not an adjective meaning angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To place two things next to each other for comparison is to set them adjacent, standing together.

clue.text: It's not among the top few journals or annuals to display

definitions.text: It's not among the top few

indicators.note: the words journals or annuals show the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Magazines and yearbooks that are shown off but never rank at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser in a race who finishes outside the placings is an also-ran, one not among the leaders.

clue.text: Carnivore from ark beaten in sporting contest

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit within the word for a sporting contest

parts.note: a meet is a sporting event, such as an athletics meet

indicators.note: beaten means battered into a new shape, so the letters of ark are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal fleeing a battered Noah's ark turns up at a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' makes RKA from the ark; a meet is the usual crossword sporting contest, as in an athletics meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The small African mongoose relative eats insects and small animals, so it is a meat-eating mammal.

clue.text: Immodest belle appearing regularly in show

indicators.note: the picked letters go within the word for show

parts.note: to indicate is to show

indicators.note: only alternate letters of belle are used, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman keeps turning up in an indecent stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes E and L from bElLe, placed inside INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate behaviour is coarse or improper, lacking modesty or tact.

clue.text: Party was triumphant

definitions.meaning: a group or gang of people working together
an old past tense of crow, to exult or boast in victory

explanation.definitionFit: A gang of people is a party; and the old past tense of crow means exulted in victory.

clue.text: Source of timber beam I overlooked in recess

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the letter I is passed over and dropped from the word for beam

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A carpenter fits a wooden beam into an alcove, ignoring himself.
explanation.walkthrough: SMILE without I gives SMLE, which 'in recess' turns back to front; 'recess' looks like an alcove but means retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: These deciduous trees are felled for their hard wood, so they are a supply of lumber.

clue.text: Deliver sermon without church's backing in unfriendly Welsh town

indicators.note: the reworked sermon word sits within the word for unfriendly

parts.note: a chilly welcome is a cold, unfriendly one

indicators.note: going backwards, so the shortened word is reversed
the letters for church are removed from the preaching word

parts.note: to preach is to deliver a sermon
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A preacher without his church's support finds a frosty reception in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the church from the sermon word, and 'backing' reverses what remains to give AERP; the unfriendly welcome is a cold one.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in south Wales, known for its castle and the crumbly cheese named after it.

clue.text: Paddy, abstainer, imbibing an alcoholic drink!

indicators.note: drinking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a person who abstains from alcohol
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A teetotaller sneaks a drink and flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy is British informal for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a fit of bad temper, an outburst like a child's.

clue.text: Character name in comic operas

indicators.note: the single letter goes within the shuffled letters
comic suggests a playful, jumbled version of the word operas

explanation.surface: A role is named in a programme for comic operas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges OPERAS into PERSOA, with N placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is an assumed role or character, the face someone presents in public.

clue.text: I'm about to take a photo, roughly 20, maybe

definitions.text: I'm about to take a photo

parts.note: say means approximately, as in say twenty people
the Welsh town at 20 across also names a crumbly white variety of this dairy food

explanation.surface: A photographer warns the group, giving a rough count of about twenty people.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' is not a number here but a cross-reference to the Welsh town at 20 across, which is also a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers say this phrase to make their subjects smile just before the shutter clicks.

clue.text: Appropriate witnesses heard

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: to witness something is to see it, so witnesses means sees

explanation.surface: Fitting testimony is given by witnesses in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb here, meaning to take over, not an adjective meaning fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate something is to take it for yourself, to grab or commandeer it.

clue.text: Florid father out of puff after game?

indicators.note: the father piece is placed following the game piece

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the letters for puff leave the word for father

parts.note: daddy is a word for father
a puff is a promotional plug, an advertisement or ad

explanation.surface: A red-faced dad is out of breath after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' looks like breath, as in out of puff, but it is a promotional plug; RU, rugby union, is the crossword's usual game.
explanation.definitionFit: A florid complexion is reddish, the healthy red colour of a flushed face.

clue.text: Business report on Home Counties nursing hospital

indicators.note: in an across clue, the report piece comes after the rest
holding inside, as a nurse holds a baby, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the counties around London lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
a report is a loud noise, like a bang

explanation.surface: A news report about a hospital in the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, so SE (South East); 'Business' is the shebang in 'the whole shebang'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole shebang means the whole affair, so the word stands for an enterprise or matter.

clue.text: Casually inspected ranks in base

indicators.note: the word for ranks goes within the word for base

parts.note: a bed is a base, as in a flower bed or seabed
rows are lines or ranks

explanation.surface: An officer casually looks over the lines of soldiers at the base.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look through items in a leisurely, unhurried way.

clue.text: See about new flag in every respect

indicators.note: around, so the bishop's seat surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and so a bishop's see
to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: A clergyman looks around at a new banner from every side.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is the crossword's usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something wholly or completely is to do it fully in every respect.

clue.text: Daughters join frolics somewhere in France

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: frolics suggests romping about, so the letters of join are rearranged

explanation.surface: Daughters join in the fun on a holiday in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frolics' jumbles the word join into IJON; the town is best known abroad for its mustard.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a city in Burgundy, eastern France, famous for its mustard.

clue.text: Six-footer's height test put off — capital unavailable

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: the capital, or first, letter is missing from the word for put off

parts.note: to deter is to put off

explanation.surface: A six-foot-tall man fails a height test because the capital is out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer is a line of verse with six metrical feet, not a tall person; DETER loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of poetry made of six metrical feet is a six-foot verse line, as in Homer.

clue.text: Matched light meal with vast amount of water

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon meal
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone pairs a snack with a huge quantity of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To be teamed with something is to be paired or matched with it.

clue.text: Packed sensational tale, apart from second supporting chapter

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the chapter letter goes on top
without, so the letter for second is left out

parts.note: a shocker is a lurid, sensational story

explanation.surface: A thrilling story, but for its second part, holds up a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOCKER without S leaves HOCKER, set beneath C; chocker is British slang for crammed full.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocker is British slang for crammed full, as in a bus that is chock-a-block.

clue.text: Was likely to produce small coat

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's coat or skin

explanation.surface: A small coat seemed likely to be produced.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelt is a British past tense of spell, and 'spelled trouble' means was likely to produce it.
explanation.definitionFit: If something spelled disaster, it signalled or was likely to bring about that outcome.

clue.text: Original 100 pounds squandered by one of the family

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: lost or wasted, so the pound letter is dropped from the family member

parts.note: a relative is a member of the family
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A relative fritters away a hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Squandering the pound sign from the family member leaves REATIVE; 'Original' is an adjective here, meaning inventive.
explanation.definitionFit: An original thinker is inventive and imaginative, coming up with new ideas.

clue.text: Unattractive male in Dickens possibly succeeded

indicators.note: the letter for male is placed within the first name

parts.note: Charles was Dickens's first name, a name shared by others, hence possibly
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: An unappealing man in a Dickens novel achieved success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickens possibly' points to the novelist's first name, CHARLES, which takes M inside and S after.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without charm lacks appeal, so it is unappealing or plain.

clue.text: Weary vagrant that's got around a great deal?

definitions.text: Weary vagrant that's got around a great deal?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters surround the phrase for a great deal
vagrant means wandering, so the letters of weary roam into a new order

parts.note: far means by a great deal, as in far better

explanation.surface: A tired tramp who has travelled widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' makes WAYER from the tired word, opened by 'that's got around'; the whole clue doubles as a description of a seasoned traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller on foot who has roamed widely fits the picture of a tired, wandering tramp.

clue.text: Daily Mail's unorthodox line lacking appeal

parts.note: a daily is a British cleaner, also called a char

indicators.note: irregular or not by the rules, so the remaining letters are rearranged
missing, so the letter for line is taken away

parts.note: the word Mail's supplies its letters, possessive included

explanation.surface: A tabloid's eccentric political line is lacking in appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is a British cleaning lady, a CHAR; MAILS loses L to give MAIS, which 'unorthodox' turns into ISMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm, the magnetic attractiveness some people have.

clue.text: Like Cyclops disheartened after maiden's flush?

indicators.note: the cyclops piece comes after the maiden letter

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: losing the heart, the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the Cyclops of Greek myth had a single eye

explanation.surface: A one-eyed giant blushes, crestfallen, after a girl's rejection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flush' is the slang for having plenty of money, not a blush.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flush is to be wealthy or well supplied with cash.

clue.text: Menacing bishop leaves in fine fettle

indicators.note: departs, so the letter for bishop goes from the word

parts.note: blooming means flourishing or healthy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A threatening bishop departs in excellent health.
explanation.definitionFit: Something looming appears in a threatening way, towering ominously.

clue.text: Crook emptied library with cunning

parts.note: a crook is a bend, so an arch

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside, keeping only the outer letters of library

explanation.surface: A villain cleared out a library slyly.
explanation.definitionFit: To act archly is to behave in a knowingly sly or mischievous way.

clue.text: Stunner struck another pose, looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a model who sat again for an artist resat

explanation.surface: A gorgeous model struck a new pose, gazing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beauty, but it is a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: This electric weapon stuns a target, so it is literally something that stuns.

clue.text: The Sound of Silence, in part

indicators.note: the word for silence is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: peace is quiet or silence

explanation.surface: A Simon and Garfunkel song title is quoted in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title The Sound of Silence is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment, a part of a whole.
